newsitem.title: USA: CME May lumber falls on pre-expiration liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CME May lumber falls on pre-expiration liquidation.

text.p: Long liquidation ahead of the May contract's expiration Thursday pushed CME May lumber futures to a sharply lower close while continued weakness in cash also weighed on other months, traders said.
Lumber closed $10.10 to $2.40 per thousand board feet lower with limitless May off most at $388.30 and July off $5.40 at $393.30 per tbf.

The long liquidation in May and pressure in other months reflected the continued steady to weak undertone to cash lumber. Although activity picked up in the cash market Tuesday, cash prices were steady at best as mills continue to look for business, traders said.
"Cash is quiet again after a better tone yesterday," one cash trader said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $384 per cwt, unchanged from last Friday and down $4 from last Wednesday. Lumber prices remained tilted downward overall, they said.

Some commercial hedging developed in May futures early and the long liquidation then took it down to its low late. Rolling of long May positions into July by RBH added to pressure near the close, pit sources added.
